name: Hanmi Semiconductor
theme: HBM TC bonders (memory-adjacent equipment; washed-out leader)
thesis: Classic washed-out-stock setup inside the hottest supply chain: Hanmi is the incumbent thermal-compression bonder supplier for HBM stacking, yet the shares roughly halved over the past year (192,300 KRW on 7 Aug vs a 426,000 KRW 52-week high) on fears that Hanwha Semitech and ASMPT would erode its SK hynix franchise. The fundamentals have gone the other way: Q2 2026 was a record (revenue 251.1bn KRW, operating profit 130.3bn KRW, 51.9% operating margin), Micron became the largest customer at 46% of Q2 revenue, and SK hynix placed its first HBM4 'Griffin' TC bonder order (44.2bn KRW, ~15 tools) in June with Digitimes reporting HBM4 orders 'rebounding' to Hanmi over Hanwha. The binary that was feared -- hybrid bonding replacing TC bonding -- has been pushed out: at Hot Chips 2026 SK hynix said hybrid bonding will not be ready for HBM4E and extended MR-MUF/TC bonding through Nvidia Rubin, lengthening the TC bonder cycle. Add HBF (high-bandwidth flash) bonder deliveries from 2H26 and a second-gen hybrid bonder due by end-2026 as free options. Confirmed facts: Q2 numbers, Micron share, SK hynix order. Rumour/analysis: 'pulls ahead of Hanwha' is trade-press reporting, not a company disclosure. Risk: Hanwha patent litigation, customer concentration, and a trailing multiple that still screens high on stale estimates.

theme: Memory packaging & test OSAT (DRAM/NAND modules, TSV DDR5, FOPLP)
